headline: Majors hold trend lines while momentum stalls; whales moving coins onto exchanges as traditional finance flows reverse.
paragraphs: The regime is split but not broken. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and BNB all trade above their 200-day simple moving averages, and four of those five (all except XRP) have golden crosses, the signal that the 50-day line has crossed above the 200-day line. Doge and ADA, the stragglers, sit below their 200-day lines and lack golden crosses, which marks them as structurally weaker. The broad picture: five of seven majors are in uptrend; two are in downtrend. That split tells you the market is not unified, but it is not collapsing either.

Momentum across all majors is neutral and fading. Every single asset in the data, from Bitcoin to ADA, shows RSI-14 hovering between 42 and 55, clustered around 50: equilibrium, neither overbought nor oversold. MACD sits below signal on all seven. This is a market at rest, not accelerating. The setup is neither stretched nor deeply oversold. When you pair this against the trend lines, you see assets that are above their long-term rails but without the velocity to push higher right now. Bitcoin is up 17.7% on the month but down 6.2% on the week; Ethereum up 28.1% on the month but down 4.8% on the week; Solana up 32.3% on the month but down 8.4% on the week. The monthly trends (the rallies that got these assets above 200-day lines in the first place) have lost momentum over the past five to seven days. This is typical behavior after a sustained run: a pause, a shake, sometimes a reset.

Derivatives positioning shows crowding on the long side and funding cost that ranges from sleepy to moderate. Bitcoin funding sits at 0.83 basis points every eight hours, which annualizes to 9.1 percent, a meaningful but not extreme carry cost for longs. ETH and XRP fund at 0.57 and 0.68 basis points per eight hours respectively. All of these are elevated enough to attract longs, but not so expensive that fresh long entry is irrational. The long-to-short ratio tells the real story: Bitcoin 1.78-to-1, Ethereum 2.18-to-1, Solana 2.27-to-1, Doge 4.81-to-1. The bigger the ratio, the more consensus there is among leveraged traders that the asset is going up. Doge's 4.81 reads as a crowded skew. Liquidations over the past hour tilted heavily toward shorts in Bitcoin and Ethereum, with $1.0M Bitcoin shorts and $1.1M Ethereum shorts wiped out against $143K and zero in long liquidations respectively. That dynamic suggests shorts are the fragile side right now, but the sample window (one hour) is too narrow to call it a regime.

The tension between flows reveals the real story. Spot ETF flows into Bitcoin and Ethereum turned negative: minus $450.4M on 15 September and minus $142.3M the same day. Over the last five sessions, Bitcoin has seen a cumulative outflow of $706.6M, a persistent drain from traditional finance. Ethereum, by contrast, shows only one day of outflow but a five-session net inflow of $200M, a contradiction that keeps the picture murky for that asset. Whale exchange flows, measured over the past 24 hours, show $81.1M net moving onto exchanges, the direction longs should fear. The detail matters: Ethereum saw $242M net move onto exchanges (heavy inflow), while Bitcoin saw $160M net move off exchanges (cold storage buying). The biggest single move was $252.5M of Ethereum moving onto Coinbase. Meanwhile, the weekly whale trend is unambiguous: three of the last four weeks show coins moving onto exchanges (weeks ending Aug 26, Sep 09, and Sep 16), totaling $2.7B inbound to trading venues. That is supply pressure building.

Stablecoin float sits at $309.5B, up 1.09 percent over the month, stable dry powder at a reasonable level. The crowd sentiment gauge reads 51, Neutral, having ranged from 41 to 74 over the past month. The Fear and Greed index and the tape are in accord here: neither fear nor euphoria dominates; money is neither rushing for exits nor lever-buying peaks. Total market cap is down 4.33 percent on the day at $2.59T, Bitcoin dominance at 58.4 percent, both modest moves in the context of month-long gains.

Watch for three conditions: first, whether the weekly whale flow pattern breaks, because three consecutive weeks of coins moving onto exchanges (even as ETF money slows) suggests growing distribution pressure; second, whether Bitcoin can reclaim above its 200-day line with real conviction (it is above now, but MACD is below signal and weekly momentum is fading, a gap worth monitoring); and third, whether funding costs for longs hold or tick lower, because sustained declines in carry cost often precede reversals. ADA's break below its 200-day line and negative month-to-date performance mark it as a leading indicator of broader weakness, so its next move deserves attention.
